title: Session projections as a required reader seam
summary: A plugin whose behaviour reads projected session state must declare the projection registry as a required dependency and wait for it; a missing registry or key is an error, never a silent default.
firstReason: Required dependencies that fail loudly are how the Go cordis port already models services; keep the rule.

title: Session observations and projection-owned client state
summary: Every exact read of a session goes through one retained observation that picks the source (live or stored) and fixes one immutable read cut; values shown to clients come from registered projections over that cut, never from client-side reconstruction.
firstReason: One consistent read cut prevents the header, events and projections from describing different moments; keep it as the read path of the Go session service.

title: Explicit-feedback-only upload through OpenTelemetry
summary: Telemetry upload is mounted in feedback-only mode for everyone: only a new explicit feedback event in a session authorizes uploading that session's history up to that point. Ordinary activity never authorizes an upload.
firstReason: Consent tied to an explicit user action is a product and privacy rule the Go design must keep.

title: Session working directory
summary: Each session has one logged effective working directory, owned by one service and changed only by host operations; tools read it from that owner, and it is not placed in the system prompt.
firstReason: One logged owner for the current directory keeps tools consistent and the prompt prefix stable; keep it.

title: Session projections and command lifecycle logging
summary: Proposal (the projection registry has since shipped upstream): a state-carrying event must hold the complete new state, never a delta; domains register pure fold functions in a host projection registry; and slash-command results are logged so they can be recovered.
firstReason: Adopt. Whole-value events with registered folds are the basis for server-rendered state in the Go UI, where the latest value can always replace the previous one.

title: Projection cache read-only face matches the lifecycle identity; the client store separates cached and sequenced rows
summary: The projection cache (saved per-session derived values such as the title) has two read paths: a listing path keyed only by facts in the session header, and a fold path that also compares the fork cut. The client keeps cached rows apart from rows that carry a real sequence number.
firstReason: After a restart forked sessions showed no title, because the listing could not supply the fork cut that the cache key demanded. The identity split is host logic and ports. The rule that a cached value never replaces a sequenced one also holds for a server-rendered list, where the host applies it.

title: Asynchronous projection registration and retained readers
summary: Registering a session projection (a value folded from the event log) returns an awaitable handle. Each domain service keeps its handles private and exposes business methods, and a retained handle stays readable while its owner's cleanup drains.
firstReason: Readers that looked up by registry key lost access the moment a plugin unloaded, although an agent still needed the state while shutting down. Handle ownership fits Go well (a value the owner closes) and supports configuration reload.

title: Serve Session-list rows from a summary key set
summary: A session-list row carries every registered client view except those its owner marks as excluded from the summary (turn outline, statistics, todos and similar), so that the list payload does not grow with log length.
firstReason: The exclusion mark is a TypeScript type-level device for a payload sent to a client store. A server-rendered list reads only the values its row template shows. The goal still applies to any list endpoint the Go API offers to SDK clients.

title: Session workspace root
summary: A session works in one directory that only host operations move. The model-facing `working_directory` tool and the `cwd` parameter of the delegation tools are removed; `header.cwd` stays the immutable original project, and a new `workspace-root/change` event records a changed checkout such as an entered worktree.
firstReason: Separating the workspace root from a model-moved cursor is what lets file views, change summaries and write boundaries follow the checkout and nothing else. The Go design can start with this model and has no stored `working-directory/change` events to ignore.

title: Recognize message quotes from Markdown text
summary: A quoted passage in a user message is ordinary Markdown blockquote text. The UI recognises it by matching the text; no separate quote index is stored with the message, so a hand-typed quote and a quote made with the composer behave the same.
firstReason: Deriving presentation from the text removes durable metadata that had to be kept in step across prompt, echo and queue. A server-rendered UI benefits directly: the Go renderer recognises the blockquote when it renders the message.

title: Trim unused SessionQuery convenience methods
summary: Proposal: remove four convenience read methods and one result type from the session query service, because no product code calls them.
firstReason: Adopt by omission: the Go query interface should offer the operations with real consumers (observations, batch titles, surface reads and traces) and add others on demand.
